news_drafts.headline: Watford forecasts £0.505m temporary accommodation overspend, recovering 25% of B&B costs against 31% budgeted
news_drafts.lead:
Watford Borough Council expects to overspend by £0.505m on temporary accommodation this year, according to its first-quarter budget monitoring (the in-year check of spending against budget), reported to Cabinet on 5 October. The budget allowed for a pressure of £0.490m, so the forecast is £0.015m higher.

The council recovers about 25% of what it pays bed-and-breakfast suppliers through rents, against 31% assumed in the budget. The paper says the income budget was set from the previous year's budget rather than actual income, and that recovery was historically closer to 35%. It puts the income pressure at about £200k and the spending pressure at about £300k. Housing completions at Sydney Road, Cygnet and Plover have been delayed, which is expected to keep numbers higher through the third quarter. Officers told the Finance Scrutiny Committee that further delay to the Northcote scheme, expected until February 2027, would add to the pressure. The council is looking for accommodation in Watford and neighbouring areas, and will refine its forecasts for the second-quarter report.

Property and asset management is forecasting a separate £0.308m overspend, mainly from £0.292m of commercial investment income not achieved. Of that, £0.172m comes from vacant units, business rates (the tax on commercial property) and fees at Watford Business Park, £0.060m from vacant units and costs at Charter Place, and £0.060m from fit-out costs and vacant units at Intu Watford. The council is using its commercial risk reserve, money set aside for this purpose, until the units are let.

news_drafts.headline: Watford's auditors set out route back to a clean opinion by 2027/28 after four disclaimed years
news_drafts.lead:
Watford Borough Council's external auditors, Azets, expect the council to receive a clean opinion on its accounts for 2027/28 at the earliest, according to a "build back" report put to the Audit Committee on 30 September 2026. An external audit is an independent check on the council's accounts. For each of the four years from 2021/22 to 2024/25 the auditors issued a disclaimed opinion, meaning they could not form reasonable assurance on the accounts. The last clean opinion was for 2020/21.

Azets' indicative timeline has 2025/26 disclaimed again, 2026/27 modified ("except for", meaning the auditor has reservations on specific areas), and 2027/28 unmodified. That assumes all planned rebuild work is completed. The auditors assess the council as at the "higher end of the risk spectrum" for the exercise, citing multiple years of disclaimers, the volume of movements in its reserves (money set aside), weaknesses in controls, and changes in key staff and systems. They say this means extensive testing of income and spending over the disclaimed years.

Estimated rebuild fees are £418,640 across 2024/25 to 2026/27: £105,305 already agreed and charged for 2024/25, £194,774 for 2025/26 and £118,561 for 2026/27. The figure for 2027/28 is still to be confirmed. All of it needs approval from Public Sector Audit Appointments, the body that sets audit fees. Azets also requires the council to keep its finance function "sufficiently resourced" for both the annual audit and the rebuild testing.

The committee also had the council's treasury management report for 2025/26, covering how it borrows and invests spare cash. Interest paid on loans was £0.95m against a £1.41m budget, and investment income was £0.94m against £0.52m budgeted, though the 3.95% return trailed the 4.05% SONIA benchmark. The report says treasury activity met its limits "with limited exceptions"; it does not set them out in the main paper.

Internal auditors reported no new high-priority recommendations in 2026/27. Some earlier recommendations have slipped, among them a golf club governance review now due 30 October 2026.

findings.paper_title: Q2 Finance Monitoring report, 24/11/2026 Finance Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The revised MRP calculation method is subject to external audit review, with a Quarter 2 MRP underspend of £1.101m, up from £0.555m at Quarter 1.
findings.detail: The MRP underspend increased because the pay award previously included in the MRP forecast was removed. The report notes the revised MRP method has not yet been signed off by external audit.
findings.matters: A change in MRP methodology under external audit review affects the underlying revenue position, and other councils making similar changes may face the same scrutiny.
findings.figures: (£1.101m) MRP underspend at Quarter 2; (£0.555m) at Quarter 1; £1.509m MRP budget
findings.quote: The revised MRP calculation method is currently subject to External audit review.

findings.paper_title: Q2 Finance Monitoring report, 24/11/2026 Finance Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The MTFS assumes the Commercial risk reserve will be used to cover the 2026/27 income shortfall while vacant units are let, and the Economic Impact Reserve is forecast to fall from £978k to £718k by 31 March 2027.
findings.detail: The report says the Commercial risk reserve is assumed to manage the short-term shortfall in income while vacant units at Aspire are let. The reserves table shows the Economic Impact Reserve drawn down during the year, but does not show a separate balance for the Commercial risk reserve.
findings.matters: Using a dedicated risk reserve to bridge a commercial income gap is a choice other councils with similar exposure will compare against, and the reserve's remaining balance determines how long it can cover the gap.
findings.figures: Economic Impact Reserve £978k at 1 April 2026 to £718k forecast at 31 March 2027; General Fund £3,954k; total reserves £70,840k forecast at 31 March 2027
findings.quote: The 2026/27 to 2028/29 MTFS includes assumptions that the Commercial risk reserve will be utilised to manage the short-term shortfall in income in 2026/27 whilst vacant units are let.

findings.paper_title: Q2 Finance Monitoring report, 24/11/2026 Finance Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The 2026/27 capital forecast is £38.349m against a £42.466m latest budget, a £4.117m reduction after review of the expenditure profile.
findings.detail: The reduction includes £0.923m for Town Hall Quarter (Delivery) and £0.500m for ICT rephased to 2027/28, and £2.464m for the Museum and Heritage Town Hall Quarter delivery project rephased into 2027/28. Housing increased by £1.508m from additional LAHF funding. The latest budget includes £13.660m carried forward from 2025/26.
findings.matters: A large capital slippage into the following year, including a major town hall project, is a delivery-timing signal that lenders and other councils track against borrowing needs.
findings.figures: £38.349m forecast; £42.466m latest budget; (£4.117m) variance; £13.660m slippage from 2025/26; £2.464m Museum and Heritage rephasing; £1.508m Housing increase
findings.quote: This is a forecast overall decrease of (£4.117m).

findings.paper_title: Q2 Finance Monitoring report, 24/11/2026 Finance Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Strategic Finance forecasts a £0.815m pressure, including £0.097m of unachievable savings and £0.199m of higher insurance costs.
findings.detail: The report says the Council's savings target sits in the strategic finance budget and is subject to redistribution to each service area. It also notes that movement of £0.472m of pay award budget to other service areas contributes to the pressure.
findings.matters: Savings that cannot be delivered are a recurring question for finance directors, and the report shows the target is held centrally pending redistribution.
findings.figures: £0.815m Strategic Finance net pressure; £0.097m unachievable savings; £0.199m insurance cost increase; £0.472m pay award budget movement

findings.paper_title: Q2 Finance Monitoring report, 24/11/2026 Finance Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Environment forecasts a £0.989m underspend, including approximately £0.400m of savings on Veolia pension contributions following the council's 2025 triennial pension review.
findings.detail: The report states the pension saving resulted from the 2025 triennial pension review and proposed reductions in pension contribution rates for the Veolia Environmental Maintenance Contract in 2025/26. Other contributors include SLM pool management and recycling kerbside cost reductions and £0.223m of SLM income under a new agency contract.
findings.matters: Pension contribution savings arising from a triennial valuation in an outsourced contract are a specific mechanism other councils with similar contracts may be able to check against their own arrangements.
findings.figures: (£0.989m) Environment underspend; approximately (£0.400m) Veolia pension saving; (£0.200m) SLM pool management; (£0.100m) recycling kerbside; (£0.223m) SLM income
findings.quote: approximately (£0.400m) savings on Veolia pension contributions

daily_post.headline: Total outstanding debt at 30 September 2026 is £0.838m, of which the paper reports 25% (£0.205m) over one year old.
daily_post.lead: The share of debt over a year old is a measure of recovery performance that other councils can compare.
